bug_semantics: ExpressEntryList block save() uses a request-controlled `$fromCIF = ($data['_fromCIF'] ?? null) === true` flag to decide whether to empty/rebuild the serialized `filterFields` (and `columns`) blob or to persist `$data['filterFields']` as-is. Form POST can only supply the string "true", which fails the strict boolean check, so the intended CIF-import path is blocked for ordinary block saves. REST API `Areas::addBlock`/`updateBlock` `json_decode()` the body, so JSON boolean true becomes PHP `true`; a rogue administrator who can add/edit blocks then stores an attacker-chosen serialized payload in `btExpressEntryList.filterFields`. Later `edit()`, `view()`, and export call `unserialize($this->filterFields)` with no `allowed_classes`, yielding PHP object injection / RCE when an administrator views or edits the block.
flaw_origin: The bypassable guard was first written in ac4e7e16808a609c1a3cf3403ef5dfb999e704ae (Michele Locati, 2025-06-30) as part of CIF import/export for `express_entry_list`: `save()` began skipping request rebuilds when `_fromCIF === true`, and `getImportData()` set `$args['_fromCIF'] = true` so already-serialized filter fields could round-trip. REST API block add/update already decoded JSON into the same `$data` array (6b2a277ff719e92b44504873f6e1c887a06d14a7, 2022-10-12). Immediate parent a498a28cebb06da891dcd5d50eabeb04b90d1aaa has no `_fromCIF` and always overwrites `filterFields` from `getFieldsFromRequest` when an entity exists. Later 9.4.8 POST emptying (167f16e480) and the `if (!$fromCIF)` reinstatement (5b9deadb39 / cherry-pick d649e41e6e) are not first-writes of this mechanism.

Immediate parent a498a28c lacks those lines (parent-tree verified).
